title: Book One · Chapter 89: The Knot That Holds
story:
Leo's group needs help with its string boat.

They put a stone on the narrow wooden pieces. The pieces move apart each time. One string is slack now. The other pulls too hard. The end piece tilts upwards.

Ronan comes over to watch. His own flat boat is drying after a test.

“I can tie that,” he says.

Leo gives him the two ends. “Then tie it.”

Ronan crosses one over the other. Dad made a new handle for their moving bag. Ronan watched Dad tie that knot. He remembers Dad's hands. But he never made a knot like it himself.

His first knot opens as soon as he pulls it.

“Our knot opens too,” Leo says.

Ronan tries again. Now he makes a hard lump. He cannot move the knot at all. The wood still slips beneath it.

Mei looks from their table. “The knot is not the whole problem.”

“We know,” Leo says. But he looks down at the wood again. He looks surprised. He is thinking about Mei's words.

Miss Wu brings a short, thick cord. It is easier to see than their thin string. She gives them two pencils to practise with. They can try the cord round those first.

The cord is too short to go round anyone's neck. They work flat on the desk, as she tells them.

Ronan makes the first crossing. Miss Wu stops his fingers before the next one.

“Watch this part.”

She shows him slowly. Then she unties it and leaves the cord. Another child has torn his paper. Miss Wu goes to help him.

Ronan tries. One end needs to go over the other. Leo watches that end. It goes under instead.

“That way,” Leo says.

Ronan wants him to stop speaking. He lets the cord drop for a moment.

“Show me with your finger. Do not pull it yet.”

Leo points. Ronan tries the crossing again. This time the knot lies flat. They pull the two ends and the knot stays in place.

They make it three times. On the third, Leo makes it while Ronan points.

The boat's wooden pieces still move too far apart. They add two narrow strips across the top, like Ronan and Mei's boat. Miss Wu checks the strips. They hold the wood together. Then the children can test it.

The pieces stay together under one stone. Leo grins. Ronan grins back. The boat belongs to Leo's group, and Ronan has still helped it work.

At home, Ronan asks Dad for a short cord. Dad finds one in the toolbox. He puts two spoons on the table for practice.

“Not the sharp tools,” he says.

Ronan makes the knot. Leo is not there to point. Ronan needs more time. He makes the knot again. It lies flat, and he shows it to Dad.

Dad tries to pull it apart. The knot holds.

“Who taught you?”

“Miss Wu showed it. Leo watched my wrong part.”

Dad nods. “Useful eyes.”

Ronan takes the spoons back to Mum. One has a thread caught round the handle. He removes the thread. Then he hands Mum the spoons. Now he can tie this kind of knot himself. He may still forget a step next time. If he does, he can ask Leo or Miss Wu.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- slack＝松弛的
- cord＝粗绳
- crossing＝交叉处
- holds＝牢固撑住

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：knot＝绳结；string＝细绳；strip＝窄木条。

## 读句提示

**Then he hands Mum the spoons.**

然后／他／把勺子递给妈妈。先取线，后递勺。

## 理解问题

1. 为什么只把结打得很紧仍解决不了木片散开？
2. Ronan怎样接受Leo的具体帮助？
